target_moa.text: Nedosiran is an LDHA-directed siRNA that reduces hepatic lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) via RNA-interference degradation of LDHA mRNA in hepatocytes (GalNAc-mediated delivery), thereby reducing hepatic oxalate production.

citations.quote: Nedosiran reduces levels of hepatic lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) via the degradation of LDHA messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) in hepatocytes through RNA interference. The reduction of
hepatic LDH by nedosiran reduces the production of oxalate by the liver, thereby reducing subsequent oxalate burden.

RIVFLOZA injection contains nedosiran, a double-stranded small interfering RNA (siRNA) with four covalently attached N-acetyl-D-galactosamine (GalNAc) residues. Nedosiran targets lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) in hepatocytes via GalNAc-mediated delivery.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (\ge20%) are injection site reactions, reported in 7 patients with PH1 (39%) on RIVFLOZA vs no patients on placebo; included erythema, pain, bruising, and rash, generally mild.

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (reported in \ge20% of patients) are injection site reactions. (6.1)

The most common adverse reactions were injection site reactions, which were reported in 7 patients with PH1 (39%) on RIVFLOZA as compared to no patients on placebo. Injection site reactions included erythema, pain, bruising, and rash and were generally mild and did not lead to discontinuation of treatment.
